chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, who said: I was narrated to by Sharif ibn Sabiq, Abu Muhammad al-Taflisi, from al-Fadl ibn Abi Qurra, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
There is no believer except that he has humor (daba'ah). I said: And what is humor? He said: Joking (muzah).
ai.seo_question: What does the term 'daba'ah' mean in the context of a believer's character according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Mani al-Akhbar*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) defining *daba'ah* as *muzah*, affirming that playfulness is an inherent trait of every believer, not merely an occasional behavior. This narration, often discussed in Shia ethical literature, counters the notion of excessive asceticism (*zuhd*) by establishing that a balanced, joyful disposition is a sign of spiritual health and social ease. It underscores the Prophetic tradition of maintaining warmth and approachability in communal interactions.
